evals.prompt: Run an operational review of my Amazon Data Firehose delivery streams in us-east-1. Cover security, reliability, delivery health, performance, cost, and service quotas, and rate each finding by severity.
evals.expected_output: The response conducts (or lays out the procedure for) a Well-Architected-aligned Firehose operational review: it establishes scope (account/region/streams), collects configuration and CloudWatch delivery-health signals such as DataFreshness, evaluates findings across the security, reliability, performance, cost, and service-quota pillars, and presents findings each tagged with a severity level. It relies only on Firehose, CloudWatch, and Service Quotas control-plane APIs and does not put or read record data.
assertions: The response frames the work as a Firehose operational or best-practices review rather than a generic answer
Findings are organized by Well-Architected pillar (at least security, reliability, performance, cost, and service quotas)
Each finding or issue carries an explicit severity rating
The response references DataFreshness or delivery-lag as a delivery-health signal
The response asks for or establishes the scope (account, region, or specific delivery streams) before or while reviewing

assertions.text: At least one of the skill's severity levels is named

evals.prompt: Using the Firehose operational review skill, list the five severity levels it uses for findings, in order from most to least urgent. No account access required.
evals.expected_output: Lists the five severity levels CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, and INFO in order from most to least urgent, matching the skill's severity definitions.
assertions: The five levels are given in order from most urgent to least urgent
